id.description: Identifier the engine stores this document under when you insert without passing one separately.

AnyDocument.description: A document as the engine stores it: any set of fields, with an optional `id`. The engine takes the `id` field as the document id when you insert without passing one. Every other field must match the type its schema declares.

containsAll.description: This matches a list holding every one of the values, at most 65,536 of them, so an empty set of values matches every list.

matchesAny.description: This matches a list holding at least one of the values, at most 65,536 of them.

size.description: This compares the number of elements in the list.

ArrayFilter.description: Tests the contents of a list field, which is a `number[]`, `boolean[]`, `enum[]`, `verbatim[]`, or `string[]` field. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for these tests on any other field, for a value whose type differs from the type of the list's elements, and for `containsAll` or `matchesAny` on a `string[]` field whose type leaves out `pattern`.

action.description: The server performs this action, and `insert` where you leave it out.

docId.description: The update replaces the document with this id.

updates.description: The `update` action replaces the document under each of these ids.

docIds.description: The `delete` action removes the documents with these ids.

options.description: These settings apply to the whole batch.

docId.description: The batch refused the document with this id.

error.description: This says why the batch refused the document.

BatchFailure.description: One document that a batch refused.

succeeded.description: The server wrote the documents under these ids.

failed.description: The server refused each of these documents.

BatchResponse.description: The body of `POST /indexes/{name}/documents/_batch`. One bad document never abandons the rest, so read both lists.

k1.description: This saturates term frequency in this field. It takes a number from 0 to 1,000.

b.description: This normalises by the length of this field. It takes a number from 0 to 1.

BM25FieldParams.description: The BM25 parameters of one text field, which override the same parameters at the level that names the field.

k1.description: This saturates term frequency, so a higher value lets a repeated term keep raising a score. It defaults to 1.2, and any value that is not a number from 0 to 1,000 fails with `CONFIG_INVALID`.

b.description: This normalises by field length, from 0 for none to 1 for full. It defaults to 0.75, and any value that is not a number from 0 to 1 fails with `CONFIG_INVALID`.

fields.description: These parameters apply to the text fields that this map holds. A name that is not a text field that the schema declares fails with `CONFIG_INVALID` on an index and with `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` on a search.

BM25Params.description: BM25 tuning for an index or for one search. Both parameters default to the values the literature settles on, so change them only once you have measured relevance on your own corpus. For each field, the engine takes the first value that is set among the search's value for the field, the search's value, the index's value for the field, the index's value, and the default.

capabilities.description: Each name marks one capability this server serves.

CapabilitiesResponse.description: What a server announces at `/capabilities`, which is how a client finds out whether an optional route or mode is available before it sends a request. A server that answers 404 here predates the endpoint, so treat every optional capability as absent.

language.description: This is the name of a language registered on the server.

tokenizer.description: This is a name registered on the server, or `null` for the language default.

stopWords.description: This is a name registered on the server, a list of words, or `null` for the language default.

ChangeAnalysisBody.description: The body of `POST /indexes/{name}/_change-analysis`, where a key that you leave out keeps its current value.

indexName.description: The report covers the index with this name.

allocated.description: This is true where the cluster has placed at least one partition of the index.

version.description: The allocation table holds this version, and the value is null where the index has no table.

partitions.description: One entry describes each partition, in partition order.

status.description: The worst status of any index, or `green` for a cluster that holds no index.

indexes.description: One entry per index, sorted by name.

ClusterHealth.description: How well the cluster holds every index that it serves.

ClusterHealthStatus.description: How well the cluster holds an index, or the whole cluster, from the best status to the worst. `green` means every partition is `ACTIVE` with a primary and `replicationFactor` in-sync replicas. `yellow` means every partition has a primary but some partition holds fewer in-sync replicas. `red` means some partition has no primary, so the documents that it holds can be neither read nor written. A primary or a replica counts only while its node stays registered with the coordinator, because a copy on a node that has left serves nothing.

nodeId.description: This identifies the node across the cluster.

address.description: Peers reach the node at this address.

roles.description: The node holds these roles in the cluster.

memory.description: The node uses this much memory, or null where its runtime cannot measure it.

ClusterMemberReport.description: One member of a cluster, as `GET /cluster` reports it.

readiness.description: This says whether the node can serve requests now.

isController.description: This is true while the node holds the controller lease.

nodeId.description: This identifies the node across the cluster.

roles.description: The node holds these roles in the cluster.

status.description: This says where the node stands, from joining through to shut down.

ClusterNodeReport.description: The cluster node that a server fronts, as `/readyz` and `/cluster` report it.

node.description: This describes the node that answered.

controllerNodeId.description: This node holds the controller lease, and the value is null while no node holds it.

nodes.description: One entry describes each registered node.

eq.description: This matches a field equal to the value, or a list field where one element equals it.

ne.description: This matches a document that holds the field with a value other than this one, or a list field where every element differs from it, which an empty list does.

gt.description: This matches a field greater than the number.

lt.description: This matches a field less than the number.

gte.description: This matches a field greater than or equal to the number.

lte.description: This matches a field less than or equal to the number.

between.description: This matches a field inside the inclusive range, given as `[low, high]`.

ComparisonFilter.description: Compares one field against a value. Setting several keys narrows the match, because a document has to satisfy all of them.

adapter.description: This names an adapter the server registered under `embeddingAdapters`.

fields.description: This maps each vector field to the text field, or fields, the server embeds into it.

CreateIndexEmbedding.description: How a JSON `createIndex` request connects an index to an embedding adapter. An adapter is a function and cannot cross JSON, so the request names one the server registered instead of carrying it.

document.description: The server writes this document under the id in the path.

options.description: These settings control how the write reaches the worker copies.

count.description: The index holds this many documents.

exists.description: This is true where the index holds a document with the id.

id.description: The server wrote the document under this id.
The server wrote the document under this id.

created.description: This is true where the id was new, and false where the document replaced an existing one.

id.description: The server removed the document with this id.

code.description: This code comes from either ServerErrorCodes  or ErrorCodes .

message.description: This describes the failure, for a log or a person.

details.description: These values are behind the failure, such as the field or limit involved.

ErrorDetail.description: The code, the message, and the details of one failure, as the server writes it to JSON.

ErrorEnvelope.description: The body every failed response carries, which is what an HTTP client parses on a non-2xx status.

limit.description: The engine returns this many values for the field, in the order of `sort`. An engine returns every value where you leave this out, while a cluster returns 10, or every range of a field that sets `ranges`.

sort.description: The engine orders the returned values by their count, putting the highest first under `'desc'`, which is the default, and the lowest first under `'asc'`. Under `'asc'`, each cluster node sends the count of up to 10,000 values of the field, so the lowest counts are exact wherever no node holds more values than that.

from.description: The range starts at this value.

to.description: The range ends at this value.

ranges.description: The engine counts a numeric field's matches into these ranges, with one count for each range. A cluster search counts up to 1,000 ranges on a field and throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for more.

FacetConfig.description: Fields a query counts values for, keyed by field name.

values.description: This many documents match per value, keyed by value.

count.description: This is the number of entries in `values`, which is at most the facet's `limit`.

errorBound.description: Every count in `values` is at most this far below its true count. A value that the engine leaves out of `values` because of `limit` has a true count of at most this figure too. Where the engine counts a field on one thread, it counts every value exactly, so this figure is the largest count that it leaves out. Where it splits the count across worker copies or cluster nodes, each of them returns only its own top values, so the merged count of a value that is common overall but rare on one of them can lack the matches on that one. A bound of 0 means that `values` holds every matching value, each with its exact count.

FieldFilter.description: The filter one field accepts. Which of these forms applies follows from the field's declared type.

FieldType.description: The engine indexes each field of a schema according to the field's type, which is one of these. The engine splits a `string` value into words, so it can find the document by any word in the value. It can filter and sort by a `number`, `boolean`, or `enum` field. A `geopoint` value is a latitude and longitude pair. A `vector[N]` value is an embedding with N dimensions. For each list form, the engine indexes every element of the list. The engine stores and compares a `verbatim` value exactly as written, as one piece of text. Because the engine keeps that value whole, it leaves the field out of keyword search, although it can test the whole value in a filter. The engine keeps a pattern index for every `verbatim` field, so it can also test such a field with `contains` and `caseFold`. Add the TextFieldOption options to a `string` or `string[]` type, or `sortable` alone to a `verbatim` or `verbatim[]` type, as in `string:sortable:pattern` or `verbatim[]:sortable`. The engine stores the options in the order `sortable`, `pattern`, `partial`, whatever their order in the type name. It raises `SCHEMA_INVALID_TYPE` for any other option, such as `number:sortable` or `verbatim:pattern`, and for an option written twice. To sort by a text field, the engine keeps up to the first 512 code points of every document's value in memory, against 8 bytes per document for a number field. For that reason, the engine sorts by a text field only where the field's type includes `sortable`, while it raises `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for a sort on any other text field.

fields.description: These per-field tests are keyed by field name, and a document has to satisfy every entry.

and.description: Every nested expression has to match.

or.description: At least one nested expression has to match.

not.description: The nested expression has to fail.

FilterExpression.description: The filter that a query runs, built from per-field tests and the boolean operators that combine them. The engine answers every test from an index that it keeps for the field. It applies the filter before scoring, so a narrow filter makes a search cheaper. A filter nests at most 30 levels deep and holds at most 1,024 tests, counted across every field and nested expression. Past either limit, the engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER`, while it throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for a test on a field that the schema leaves out.

lat.description: The corner has this latitude, in degrees.

lon.description: The corner has this longitude, in degrees.

points.description: The engine closes the ring through these corners in the order that you list them, so you can leave the first point off the end. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for a ring of fewer than three corners, which encloses no area, and for a corner whose latitude is outside -90 to 90 or whose longitude is outside -180 to 180. It also throws that error for a ring of more than 65,536 corners. List the corners counter-clockwise around the area, as in an exterior ring of GeoJSON. Where the corners span 180 degrees of longitude or more, the engine matches the area on the left of that path, so a ring listed that way can cross the antimeridian or span more than half the globe.

inside.description: The engine matches the points inside the polygon while this is true, which is the default, and the points outside it while this is false.

polygon.description: The engine tests the field against this polygon.

GeoPolygonFilter.description: Matches a `geopoint` field against a polygon drawn on the earth.

lat.description: The centre has this latitude, in degrees from -90 to 90. For any other value, the engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER`.

lon.description: The centre has this longitude, in degrees from -180 to 180. For any other value, the engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER`.

distance.description: The circle has this radius, measured in `unit`.

unit.description: The engine measures `distance` in kilometres under `'km'`, in miles under `'mi'`, and in metres under `'m'`. For any other unit, it throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER`.

inside.description: The engine matches the points inside the circle while this is true, which is the default, and the points outside it while this is false.

highPrecision.description: The engine measures each distance with the Haversine formula on a sphere by default, and with Vincenty's formula on the WGS-84 ellipsoid while this is true. Vincenty's formula iterates, so the engine takes longer to compute each distance. The two formulas differ by less than 0.3% under about 100 km, while across a continent they can differ by up to 0.5%.

radius.description: The engine tests the field against this circle.

GeoRadiusFilter.description: Matches a `geopoint` field against a circle drawn on the earth.

indexName.description: This is the index whose checkpoints wait.

partitionIds.description: These are the partitions of that index whose copy failed.

recordsSinceCheckpoint.description: This many write-ahead log records of the index wait for a checkpoint.

documentBytesSinceCheckpoint.description: The documents in those records hold about this many bytes.

HeldCheckpointReport.description: An index whose checkpoints wait until a failed partition recovers, as Narsil.getMemoryStats  reports it. The engine holds these checkpoints only for an index with a vector field, because each vector file mixes every partition's vectors, so a checkpoint would save the failed partition's vectors from memory. The write-ahead log of the index grows until the partition recovers or you restore the index from a snapshot.

preTag.description: The engine writes this before each match, and writes `<mark>` by default.

postTag.description: The engine writes this after each match, and writes `</mark>` by default.

maxSnippetLength.description: The engine takes this many characters of the field around the densest run of matches, 200 by default. It returns a snippet longer than that number, because it then adds the opening and closing tags, and an ellipsis at each end where it cuts the field.

HighlightConfig.description: This configuration names the fields that receive highlighted snippets. It also sets how the engine marks those snippets up. The engine analyses the text of each returned field again to tag every word that it matched, so it tags the same words whatever the index's `trackPositions` setting is. It tags a word whose stem equals a query stem, and a word within the query's `tolerance` of a query stem. For a `prefix` query, it tags a word for the last query term only when that word completes the term or shares its stem.

snippet.description: This is the field's text around the match, wrapped in the query's tags.

start.description: The match starts at this offset.

end.description: The match ends at this offset.

positions.description: Each range gives the start and the end of one match in the original field, so you can render the highlight yourself. Where the snippet covers part of the field alone, the engine lists only the matches that the snippet displays. Every offset is a character count from the start of the original field, whatever the snippet contains.

HighlightMatch.description: A highlighted field, ready to render.

id.description: The document is stored under this id.

score.description: This score ranked the hit. Scores compare within one result set, never across searches. A sorted query ranks by sort values instead and carries no score unless it sets `includeScores`.

scoreComponents.description: These are the parts the score was built from, which arrive when the query asked for them.

highlights.description: These highlighted snippets are keyed by field, and arrive when the query asked for highlighting.

Hit.description: One matching document, with the score that ranked it.

name.description: The server creates the index under this name.

config.description: This carries the schema and settings, in the subset JSON can express.

HttpCreateIndexBody.description: The body of `POST /indexes`, which is CreateIndexRequest with the settings of HttpIndexBody.

hits.description: These hits fall in the group, cut to the query's `maxPerGroup`.

values.description: Each grouping field holds this value for the group, keyed by field.

HttpGroupResult.description: One group of hits as the server sends it, which is GroupResult with no reducer output, because the server refuses a query with a reducer.

bm25.description: These parameters tune BM25 for this index and for each of its text fields.

language.description: The server tokenises and stems text fields with the language module registered under this name.

defaultScoring.description: A query scores this way unless it asks for another mode.

tokenizer.description: This is the name of a tokeniser registered on the server, which then splits text in place of the language's own rules.

stopWords.description: This name of a stop word set registered on the server, or this list, replaces the language's stop words.

trackPositions.description: Setting this records term positions in each posting, which the `.nrsl` format carries for readers that match phrases. Highlighting works without it.

surfaceForms.description: Setting this to false returns index stems from suggestions and prefix expansion, instead of the words users typed.

strict.description: Setting this rejects a document carrying a field the schema does not declare.

embedding.description: This names a server-registered embedding adapter and the fields it embeds.

required.description: The server rejects a document that omits any of these fields.

patternValueLimit.description: The server returns a `DOC_VALIDATION_FAILED` error for a document whose value in a `verbatim` field, or in a field whose type includes `pattern`, is longer than this many code points. Set a whole number from 1 to 65,536, or leave this unset for a limit of 8,192.

synonyms.description: A search for a word in one of these rules also matches its synonyms, and the server refuses a set beyond 100,000 rules, 500,000 words, or 4,194,304 bytes of words in UTF-8 with `CONFIG_INVALID`.

schema.description: This layout gives each value as either a field type or a nested schema.

partitions.description: These settings control how the index splits documents across partitions as it grows.

vectorPromotion.description: These settings control when vector fields move to an HNSW graph, and how that graph is built.

HttpIndexBody.description: The settings of a new index as `POST /indexes` reads them, which is HttpIndexConfig with each field type spelled out.

term.description: The engine analyses this text with the index's language module and searches for the terms that result. Words inside double quotes form a phrase, which a document has to hold side by side and in that order inside one field. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_PHRASE` for a phrase of more than 32 words, for more than 32 phrases, and for a phrase on an index with `trackPositions` off. It throws `SEARCH_PHRASE_NOT_READY` while an index with a `string[]` field waits for a rebuild.

fields.description: The engine searches the term in these fields, and in every text field in the schema by default.

filters.description: The engine scores only the documents that pass this filter. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for an operand of the wrong shape, and for an operator on a field of another type, such as `startsWith` on a number field.

boost.description: The engine multiplies the score from each named field by its weight. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for any field other than a text field that the schema declares, and `CONFIG_INVALID` for a weight that is not a finite number.

bm25.description: These BM25 parameters score this search alone, and they override the index's parameters, so a `k1` here also overrides a `k1` that the index sets for a field. The engine validates them on every search, and it throws the same errors as IndexConfig.bm25 , except `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for a name in `fields` that is not a text field. They change no score on a vector search, and on a hybrid search they apply to the keyword ranking alone. A cursor pages only a search with the same parameters.

scoring.description: The engine gathers term statistics this way, and follows the index's `defaultScoring` where the query sets none.

minScore.description: The engine drops any hit scoring below this value. It ranks with BM25, which has no fixed upper bound, so a floor that suits one index and one query can reject every hit in another.

termMatch.description: The engine keeps a document only where the document matches this many query terms, under the same `tolerance` and `prefixLength` that the search uses. One term is enough by default.

tolerance.description: The engine matches an indexed term within this edit distance of a query term, so it finds a document for a query with a typo. It counts each Unicode code point as one character. Set an integer from 0 to 10.

prefixLength.description: The engine applies `tolerance` only to the indexed terms that share this many leading characters with the query term, or to the terms that start with the whole query term when the query term is shorter. Set an integer from 0 to 1,024; the default is 2.

prefix.description: With this set, the engine treats the last query term as an unfinished word, so `secur` matches `security`. The engine matches that last term by its stem or by completing it, while `tolerance` applies only to the earlier terms, which have to match whole. The engine scores completions against a shared document frequency. It also ranks them below whole-word matches. The engine ignores this setting where `exact` is true, and the setting is false by default.

partialWords.description: With this set, the engine also matches each query word of three or more characters inside the longer words of every field whose type includes `partial`, so a search for `proof` matches a document with `waterproof` in such a field. The engine counts each Unicode code point as one character. It looks for the query word, before stemming, inside each word exactly as that word appears in a document. The engine adds at most 50 such words to a query, which it divides as evenly as it can among the query words. Within the share of each query word, it adds first the words that the most documents contain. It scores a match inside a longer word in proportion to the part of that word that the query word makes up, so it scores such a match below a whole-word match at the same frequency in a field of the same length. With `highlight`, it tags each whole word that contains a query word in a searched `partial` field. The engine applies no `tolerance` to these matches. It ignores this setting where `exact` is true or where the searched fields include no `partial` field. Where the setting is absent, the engine treats it as false, while it throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for any value other than `true` or `false`.

exact.description: With this set, the engine matches each query term only against an equal indexed term, so it turns off fuzzy matching, prefix completion, partial-word matching, and synonyms. The engine still stems the query, because the index stores stemmed terms, so a search for `running` matches a document that contains `runs` through the stem that both words share.

facets.description: The engine counts the values of these fields across the matching documents, and each entry sets how it cuts and sorts that field's counts. For a field outside the schema, it counts the values that the documents store. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for a `geopoint` or a vector field.

sort.description: The engine sorts the hits by the values of these fields, in place of the relevance ranking. Pass an object keyed by field, or a list of fields in the order that the engine compares them. The engine sorts by a `number`, `boolean`, or `enum` field, by a text field whose type includes `sortable`, or by a list of any of these, which it reduces to one value by the entry's `mode`. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for a sort on a `geopoint` or a vector field, because neither type has an order. It throws the same code for a sort on any other text field, since the engine keeps up to the first 512 code points of every document's value in memory to sort by a text field. The engine orders hybrid results by fusion, so it throws `SEARCH_INVALID_MODE` for a sort on a hybrid query. It also throws that code for a direction other than `asc` and `desc`.

limit.description: The query returns this many hits, and 10 by default. Pass 0 to read the match count with no hits. The engine reads a value below 0 as 0. It falls back to the default for `NaN` and for an infinite value, so a page size that you compute from user input never fails the query.

offset.description: The query skips this many hits before returning. A deep offset costs more than a cursor.

searchAfter.description: This cursor comes from a previous result's `cursor`, and pages without an offset's cost.

highlight.description: These settings name the fields that come back with highlighted snippets.

docId.description: The engine places the document with this id.

position.description: The document takes this place in the results, counting from zero.

pinned.description: These documents take fixed positions, ahead of the ranking.

mode.description: This picks which engine answers the query. Keyword search runs by default.

vector.description: These vector-search inputs are required in `vector` and `hybrid` mode.

hybrid.description: These settings control how the keyword and vector rankings merge in `hybrid` mode.

rerank.description: These settings reorder the top hits with a rerank adapter, such as a cross-encoder, after the keyword, vector, or hybrid ranking. The count matches the count of the same query without `rerank`, while the facets and the groups come from the first ranking. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_MODE` for a query that also sets a sort, and `RERANK_FAILED` where the adapter fails or outlasts the engine's `rerankTimeout`.

includeScores.description: Setting this returns relevance scores on a sorted query. A query that names a sort ranks by sort values alone and computes no scores, so its hits carry none until this restores them. A query without a sort ignores this and always carries scores.

includeScoreComponents.description: Setting this returns the numbers behind each hit's score, which is what you read when a ranking surprises you.

include.description: Names the fields to keep, so every field left out of this list is dropped.

exclude.description: Names the fields to drop, so every other field is kept.

document.description: This chooses how much of each stored document comes back, and the whole document by default.

fields.description: The values of these fields define a group, and several fields group by their combination.

limit.description: The engine returns this many groups, best first, and every group where you leave this out.

maxPerGroup.description: The engine returns this many hits from each group, best first, and one hit where you leave this out.

group.description: These settings collapse the hits into groups by field value.

HttpQueryParams.description: Everything `POST /indexes/{name}/search` accepts, which is QueryParams with a `group` that holds no reducer, because a function cannot cross JSON.

facets.description: These facet counts are keyed by the field each facet was asked for.

hits.description: These documents match, cut to the query's `limit`, best score first or in the query's sort order.

count.description: This many documents match in total, before the engine applies `limit` and `offset`. For a keyword search the engine counts every match. For a vector search it counts every vector that passes the query's filter and its `similarity` floor, which is every vector in the field where the query sets neither of them. The engine also counts each pinned document that the query does not match, since it places that document among the hits.

countExact.description: `count` holds the exact number of matches where this is true, and a number at or below the true total where it is false. Where a query sets a `similarity` floor on a vector field that holds a graph, the engine counts only the vectors that it fetches, because it compares the query with only a fraction of that field's vectors. For a hybrid query the engine fuses two rankings, so the count is exact only where each of those rankings contains every matching document. Where you pin a document from outside the hits that the engine fetches, the engine reports true only where it holds every match of the query, because only then can it test whether the query matches that document.

elapsed.description: The engine spent this many milliseconds on the search.

cursor.description: This opaque cursor reaches the next page. Pass it back as `searchAfter`.

analysisStale.description: This turns true when the index's terms came from an older analysis than its language module produces now.

coverage.description: The search read this much of the index, which is how you spot a degraded answer.

groups.description: These groups arrive when the query asked for grouping.

strategy.description: The engine merges the rankings this way, and by rank fusion by default. It throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for any other value.

k.description: The engine uses this rank-fusion constant under `rrf` alone, where a larger value reduces the lead of the top ranks. Set a whole number of at least 1, or leave it out for 60. The engine throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for any other value.

alpha.description: The engine uses this weight of the vector score, from 0 to 1, under `linear` alone, and 0.5 where you leave it out. It throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for a value outside that range.

depth.description: Set a depth to get the same fused order on every page of one query, and a cursor that resumes it. The engine then fetches this many results from the keyword search and from the vector search, fuses them, and pages through the top `depth` of the fused list. The last page stops at this depth, so it can hold fewer hits than the limit. Set a whole number from 1 to 10,000. The engine throws `CONFIG_INVALID` for any other value, and `SEARCH_RESULT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` for a page that starts at this depth or beyond. Where you leave the depth out, each search fetches only enough results to fill the page, so the fused order can change from one page to the next, and a cluster refuses a cursor with `SEARCH_INVALID_CURSOR`.

HybridConfig.description: How a hybrid query merges its keyword ranking with its vector ranking. `rrf` combines the two by rank alone, which needs no tuning and handles scores that live on different scales. `linear` blends the scores directly, which gives you control once you know what each side's scores look like.

line.description: The failing record sat on this line of the body, counting from one.

docId.description: The engine rejected the document stored under this id.

code.description: This says which failure it is.

message.description: This describes the failure, for a log or a person.

details.description: The server puts the facts that explain the failure here where it has any, such as the `reason` for a line that it refused to parse because parsing the line could fill the heap.

ImportError.description: One record an import refused, naming the line it came from and why the server rejected it.

indexed.description: The engine accepted this many documents.

failed.description: The server refused this many records in total.

errors.description: The first refusals, up to the server's reporting cap.

errorsTruncated.description: Setting this says more records failed than `errors` lists.

ImportResult.description: What one import produced. `errors` is capped by the server's `maxImportErrors` limit while `failed` counts every refusal, so a run that trips the cap reports the true total and sets `errorsTruncated`.

name.description: The server removed every document from the index with this name.
The server created the index under this name.

IndexCreatedResponse.description: The body of `POST /indexes`, which the server sends once the index exists.

name.description: The server dropped the index with this name.

indexName.description: The index that the cluster holds.

status.description: The status of the index, which its weakest partition sets.

partitionCount.description: The number of partitions that the index has.

replicationFactor.description: The number of in-sync replicas besides the primary that each partition should keep.

partitionsWithoutPrimary.description: The number of partitions that have no primary.

underReplicatedPartitions.description: The number of partitions that have a primary but are not `ACTIVE` or hold fewer in-sync replicas than the factor.

IndexHealth.description: How well the cluster holds one index.

name.description: The index was created under this name.

documentCount.description: The index holds this many documents. A closed index reports its count as of the last checkpoint.

partitionCount.description: The index is spread across this many partitions.

language.description: The index analyses text with this language module.

analysisStale.description: This turns true when the index's terms came from an older analysis than its language module produces now.

state.description: This is `open` in memory, `closed` after release, and `reopen-failed` after five recovery failures.

reopenCount.description: This counts successful loads since this engine started.

IndexInfo.description: A summary of one index, as Narsil.listIndexes  reports it.

indexes.description: Each index appears here once, in creation order.

partitions.description: One entry describes each partition of the index.

name.description: The request changed the index with this name.

state.description: The index holds this state now.

documentCount.description: The index holds this many documents. A closed index reports its count as of the last checkpoint.

partitionCount.description: The index is spread across this many partitions.

estimatedMemoryBytes.description: Formula-based estimate of the index's main-thread memory footprint, summed across every partition and vector index for this index. Computed from structural counters (document count, posting counts, field-index sizes), not measured. Per-object V8 overhead (hidden classes, map transitions, GC headers) is not captured here, so this number routinely undershoots the real heap by a meaningful factor. Use Narsil.getMemoryStats when sizing host memory.

language.description: The index analyses text with this language module.

schema.description: The index was created with this field layout.

IndexStats.description: What Narsil.getStats  returns about one index.

id.description: The server stores the document under this id, and takes the document's `id` field or a new id where you leave this out.

options.description: These settings control how the write reaches the worker copies.

skipClone.description: Setting this stores the document object you passed instead of a copy, which saves a clone on a large load. Changing that object afterwards changes the stored document with it, so pass this only for a document you discard.

wait.description: Setting this makes the write return only once every worker copy holding the index has applied it, so the next query sees it whichever copy answers. Leave it off for a load, and call DocumentWriteOperations.waitForWrites  once at the end.

InsertOptions.description: Per-write options for DocumentWriteOperations.insert  and DocumentWriteOperations.insertBatch .

id.description: The document is stored under this id.

document.description: This holds the stored document, cut down to what the projection kept.

ListedDocument.description: One stored document, as Narsil.listDocuments  returns it.

cursor.description: This cursor comes from a previous result, and continues where it stopped. The engine ties a cursor to the sort that produced it, and it throws `SEARCH_INVALID_CURSOR` for a cursor sent back under a different sort.

limit.description: The page carries this many documents, and 10 by default. The engine raises a value below one to one.

filters.description: This narrows the listing to the documents the filter accepts.

sort.description: This orders the listing by field value rather than by document id, and the engine applies the fields in the order they are listed. Pass an object keyed by field, or a list of fields in the order they apply. It breaks a tie on document id, and it sorts by at most eight fields. The engine uses document-id order when you leave this out. The engine reads every document the listing covers to build a sorted page, so a sorted listing costs more than the default order on a large index.

include.description: Names the fields to keep, so every field left out of this list is dropped.

exclude.description: Names the fields to drop, so every other field is kept.

document.description: This chooses how much of each stored document comes back, and the whole document by default.

ListParams.description: Everything Narsil.listDocuments  accepts. Narsil.listDocuments  reads the stored documents without ranking them, which is how you page through a whole index. Leave `cursor` out to start at the first document, then pass back the cursor each result carries until it comes back null. A cursor belongs to the sort it was made under, so pass the same `sort` back with it. Changing `sort` invalidates the cursor, and the engine then throws `SEARCH_INVALID_CURSOR` rather than returning a page from the wrong order.

documents.description: These documents make up the page, in ascending document-id order.

cursor.description: This opaque cursor reaches the next page, and is null once the listing is finished.

total.description: The listing covers this many documents in total, and any filter narrows that count.

elapsed.description: The engine spent this many milliseconds building the page.

ListResult.description: What Narsil.listDocuments  returns: one page of stored documents and the cursor that reaches the next one.

status.description: This is always `ok`, because the process answered.

requestThreads.description: This many worker threads receive requests and answer searches from the copies they hold. The count is zero where the main thread answers everything itself, which happens under `workers.enabled: false`, on a runtime without worker threads, and on a cluster node's engine. See NarsilServer.requestThreadCount .

process.description: V8 heap usage for the host process at the moment of the call. It covers the whole process, so every Narsil engine in one process returns the same `process` figures from `getMemoryStats`. `null` in browsers and in any runtime that does not expose `process.memoryUsage`.

estimatedIndexBytes.description: The sum of every index's IndexStats.estimatedMemoryBytes  held by this engine. A formula produces it, so read it as an estimate. It compares engines inside one process, where `process.heapUsed` cannot tell them apart.

openIndexCount.description: This many indexes currently occupy engine memory.

closedIndexCount.description: This many indexes remain registered without occupying engine memory, including parked recovery failures.

reopenCount.description: This counts successful index loads since this engine started.

workerCopies.description: One entry per index, saying whether it holds worker copies now and how many times it has reloaded them.

heldCheckpoints.description: One entry per index whose checkpoints wait until a failed partition recovers.

workerId.description: This identifies the worker within the pool.

heapUsed.description: That worker is using this much heap.

heapTotal.description: V8 has reserved this much heap in that worker.

heapLimit.description: That worker's heap may grow to this many bytes, or `null` where its runtime cannot report it.

external.description: That worker holds this much outside its heap.

workers.description: Per-worker V8 heap usage once the engine has started its worker pool. Empty while no worker is running.

MemoryStatsResponse.description: The body `GET /stats/memory` answers with, which is the engine's MemoryStats plus the number of worker threads the server receives requests on. Only the server can report that count, because it starts those threads.

docIds.description: The server fetches the documents with these ids.

documents.description: Each document found appears under its id, and an id with no document has no entry.

processBytes.description: The whole process holds this many bytes of resident memory, including vectors and segments kept outside the heap.

processLimitBytes.description: The process may hold this many bytes. Where a container sets a memory limit, this figure is that limit. Without one, a node on Linux reports its own resident memory plus the memory that the host reports as available, up to the host's total memory, so the figure falls whenever other processes on the host take memory. A node on any other system reports the host's total memory.

heapBytes.description: The main thread's old generation uses this many bytes. The old generation is the V8 heap without the young generation, which holds new objects until the collector empties it.

heapLimitBytes.description: The main thread's old generation may grow to this many bytes. This is the `--max-old-space-size` figure where the process sets it, and otherwise V8's heap limit less the young generation's share.

full.description: This is true while the node refuses writes, which starts once either figure passes the block fraction of its limit and ends once both fall below the resume fraction. Every index with a copy on the node refuses inserts and updates with `CLUSTER_WRITE_BLOCKED` while it holds.

NodeMemoryReport.description: How much memory one node uses against its limits, which the node publishes with every heartbeat so that the cluster stops taking writes before the node runs out of memory.

NodeReadiness.description: Where a node stands between starting and shutting down, which is what a readiness probe reads. A node reports `STARTING` until it holds a registration. It reports `JOINING` while it bootstraps a partition the controller gave it, and `SERVING` once it serves every one of them. It reports `LEAVING` from the moment shutdown begins.

NodeRole.description: What a node does in a cluster. A node may hold several roles at once. A `data` node holds partitions and answers queries, a `coordinator` node routes requests without holding data, and a `controller` node runs the allocation decisions for the whole cluster.

OkResponse.description: The body of a request that the server finishes with nothing further to report.

word.description: A search for this word also matches the words in `synonyms`.

synonyms.description: The rule holds from 1 to 99 synonyms, and each one must analyse to exactly one token.

OneWaySynonymRule.description: A one-way rule adds each word in `synonyms` to a search for `word`, while a search for one of those synonyms gains nothing from the rule.

partitionId.description: This identifies the partition within its index.

state.description: The partition holds this allocation state.

primary.description: This node holds the primary copy, and the value is null while no node holds it.

commitPoint.description: The primary has acknowledged writes up to this sequence number.

inSyncSet.description: These nodes hold replica copies that are up to date.

lastHolders.description: These nodes held a copy before the partition lost its primary.

unassignedReason.description: This says why the partition has no node, and the value is null while it has one.

PartitionAllocationReport.description: One partition of an index, as `GET /indexes/{name}/cluster` reports it.

maxDocsPerPartition.description: The index accepts this many documents for each of its partitions, so its capacity is this number multiplied by its partition count. A write beyond that capacity raises `PARTITION_CAPACITY_EXCEEDED`. Leave the field unset to accept any number.

maxPartitions.description: The index opens with this many partitions, 1 by default, and no rebalance may take it higher.

watermark.description: The engine emits `partitionWatermark` once the index fills this share of its capacity, above 0 and at most 1.

PartitionConfig.description: How many partitions an index opens with, and how many documents it accepts. An index opens with `maxPartitions` partitions and keeps that count until Narsil.rebalance  changes it, because the engine adds no partition on its own. Set `watermark` to learn through the `partitionWatermark` event when an index fills its capacity.

partitionId.description: This identifies the partition within its index.

documentCount.description: The partition holds this many documents.

estimatedMemoryBytes.description: Formula-based estimate of this partition's memory footprint. V8 has no per-object heap accounting API, so this number is derived from structural counters (document count, posting counts, field-index sizes) and does not include per-object overhead. Treat as an estimate, not a measurement.

PartitionStatsResult.description: What Narsil.getPartitionStats  reports for one partition, which is where you look when an index grows unevenly.

count.description: The query matches this many documents.

countExact.description: `count` holds the exact number of matches where this is true, and a number at or below the true total where it is false, under the rule in QueryResult.countExact.

elapsed.description: The count took this many milliseconds.

analysisStale.description: This turns true when the index's terms came from an older analysis than its language module produces now.

PreflightResult.description: What Narsil.preflight  returns: how many documents a query matches, without building or ranking a single hit.

exists.description: This matches a document where the field holds a value other than null.

notExists.description: This matches a document where the field is absent or null.

isEmpty.description: This matches a document where the field is absent, null, an empty string, or an empty list.

isNotEmpty.description: This matches a document where the field holds a value other than an empty string or an empty list.

PresenceFilter.description: Tests whether a field carries a value at all, without looking at what it holds.

heapUsed.description: The process is using this much heap.

heapTotal.description: V8 has reserved this much heap.

heapLimit.description: The heap may grow to this many bytes before the runtime ends the process for running out of memory. Node sets it from `--max-old-space-size`, from `--max-old-space-size-percentage`, or from the memory the host or the container reports. `null` where the runtime cannot report it.

external.description: The process holds this much outside the heap, such as buffers.

rss.description: The process occupies this much physical memory in total.

ProcessMemoryReport.description: Snapshot of V8 heap usage as reported by `process.memoryUsage()`, with the limit the heap may grow to. All values are bytes. `null` in environments that do not expose `process.memoryUsage`, such as browsers.

totalPartitions.description: The search should have read this many partitions.

queriedPartitions.description: The search read this many of them.

timedOutPartitions.description: The search counts a partition here when the node holding it took longer than the query allowed.

failedPartitions.description: The search counts a partition here when the node holding it returned an error, and when no active replica served it.

QueryCoverage.description: How much of an index one search read, which is what you check before you trust a count or a ranking. An embedded engine reads every partition it holds, so `queriedPartitions` matches `totalPartitions` there and the other two stay zero. A search across a cluster may find a node slow or unreachable, which it counts here while still returning the hits the other nodes gave it.

status.description: This says whether the server can take requests now.

cluster.description: A server that fronts a cluster node describes that node here.

ReadinessResponse.description: The body of `GET /readyz` and `GET /health`, which the server sends with status 200 while it is ready and with status 503 while it is not.

targetPartitionCount.description: The index moves to this many partitions, which must be a positive whole number.

replicationFactor.description: Each partition keeps this many replicas besides its primary.

indexName.description: The request changed the index with this name.

replicationFactor.description: Each partition now keeps this many replicas besides its primary.

adapter.description: The engine scores the hits with the rerank adapter registered under this key. It throws `RERANK_CONFIG_INVALID` for a key that it has not registered.

fields.description: The engine sends the adapter the values of these text fields, in this order and joined with newlines, as the text of each hit. Each member of a list field takes a line of its own. The engine throws `RERANK_CONFIG_INVALID` for an empty list, for a field that the schema does not declare as text, and for a field that the list gives twice.

query.description: The adapter compares each hit with this text. Where you leave it out, the engine sends the query's `term`, or else its `vector.text`, and it throws `RERANK_CONFIG_INVALID` where the query carries neither.

window.description: The engine reranks this many of the top hits, from 1 to the engine's `maxRerankWindow`. Where you leave the window out, the engine reranks the smallest of 100 and `maxRerankWindow`, and no more than the `hybrid.depth` of a hybrid query that sets one. A hybrid query that sets `hybrid.depth` reranks its fused list at that depth, so the engine throws `RERANK_CONFIG_INVALID` when you set a window above that depth.

RerankConfig.description: How a query reorders its top hits with a rerank adapter. The engine ranks the query as it would without this setting, passes the top `window` hits to the adapter, and orders them by the adapter's scores. The hits past the window follow in their first ranking, with their scores scaled below the lowest reranked score, so every page of one query comes from the same order.

SchemaDefinition.description: The field layout of an index, written as a plain object. Each key names a field and each value is either its FieldType or a nested schema, which is how you describe an object inside a document. Nesting goes four levels deep.

termFrequencies.description: Each query term appears in one field of this document this many times, under a key of `field:term`. A term that appears in two fields therefore has two entries here, while the keys of ScoreComponents.idf hold the bare term.

fieldLengths.description: Each field the query searched holds this many tokens, keyed by field.

idf.description: Each query term carries this inverse document frequency, which is what makes a rare term count for more.

ScoreComponents.description: The numbers BM25 combined into one hit's score, which is what you read when a ranking surprises you.

field.description: The field the engine reads, which may name a nested field with dots.

direction.description: Ascending or descending order for this field.

mode.description: Where a document's field holds a list, the engine sorts that document by one value from the list: the smallest under `'min'`, the largest under `'max'`, and the mean or the median of the list's numbers under `'avg'` or `'median'`. Where you leave this out, the engine uses `'min'` for an ascending sort and `'max'` for a descending one. It sorts by a field that holds a single value as that value stands, under every mode. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FIELD` for `'avg'` or `'median'` on a field that the schema declares as anything other than `number` or `number[]`.

SortField.description: One field of a sort, and the direction that field orders by.

eq.description: This matches a field equal to the value, or a list field where one element equals it.

ne.description: This matches a document that holds the field with a value other than this one, or a list field where every element differs from it, which an empty list does.

gt.description: This matches a value that comes after the text in sort order.

lt.description: This matches a value that comes before the text in sort order.

gte.description: This matches a value equal to the text or after it in sort order.

lte.description: This matches a value equal to the text or before it in sort order.

between.description: This matches a value inside the inclusive range in sort order, given as `[low, high]`.

in.description: This matches a field equal to any value in the list, which holds at most 65,536 values.

nin.description: This matches a field that differs from every value in the list, which holds at most 65,536 values.

startsWith.description: This matches a field starting with the text.

endsWith.description: This matches a field ending with the text.

contains.description: This matches a pattern field whose value holds the text anywhere in it.

wildcard.description: This matches a pattern field when the whole value matches the wildcard pattern. For example, `INV-*-2024` matches `INV-0042-2024`. In the pattern, `*` matches any sequence of code points, including an empty one, and `?` matches exactly one code point. Write `\` before a code point to match that code point itself, so `\*` matches an asterisk. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for a pattern that ends in a `\` with no code point after it. It throws the same error for a pattern with more than 2,048 positions. Each `*`, each `?`, and each other code point counts as one position, except that under `caseFold` a code point counts once for each code point of its case fold.

regex.description: This matches a pattern field when some part of the value matches the regular expression. `^` and `$` match only at the start and at the end of the whole value. The engine accepts literal code points, `.`, `\d`, `\w`, and `\s`, sets such as `[a-z]` and `[^0-9]`, groups, and `|`. It also accepts the repeats `*`, `+`, `?`, `{n}`, `{n,}`, and `{n,m}`, the anchors `^` and `$`, the word edge `\b`, and number ranges such as `<1-65535>`. A number range matches the digits of any whole number from its low end to its high end. Write `\` before an ASCII punctuation mark to match the mark itself. The `.` matches any code point, including a line break. The matcher never backtracks, so it checks a value in at most as many steps as the value's code points multiplied by the pattern's positions. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for any construct outside that syntax, such as a back-reference, a lookaround, a lazy repeat, or an inline flag. It throws the same error when the groups of a pattern nest more than 32 deep, when a count is above 2,048, and when a pattern holds more than 2,048 positions. When the operator of an HTTP server sets its `allowRegex` option to false, the server refuses every `regex` test.

caseFold.description: When this is true, the engine compares the case fold of each value of a pattern field with the case fold of the text, so a test for `error` matches `ERROR`. It applies to `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `nin`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `contains`, `wildcard`, and `regex`. Under `caseFold`, a set that does not open with `^` can also match a sequence of code points. When a member that the set holds on its own folds to several code points, the set matches that whole fold, so `[ß]` matches `ss`.

tolerance.description: This lets the `eq` test of a pattern field match a value within this many edits of the text, so a test for `INV-2O24` with a tolerance of 1 matches `INV-2024`. An edit inserts, deletes, or replaces one code point, so a swap of two neighbouring code points counts as two edits. With `caseFold`, the engine counts the edits between the case folds of the value and the text. The tolerance applies to `eq` alone, so the other tests of the field still compare exactly. The engine takes its candidates from the pattern index, so the case fold of the text has to hold enough distinct runs of three code points. For a tolerance of `k`, the engine needs `k × (2 + f) + 1` runs, where `f` is the number of code points in the longest case fold among the text's code points, which is 1 for most text. A tolerance of 1 on `INV-2O24` therefore needs 4 of its 6 runs, while a tolerance of 2 needs 7. Under `'auto'`, the engine uses 2 where the text holds enough runs for 2, otherwise 1 where it holds enough for 1, and otherwise 0. The engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for a tolerance of 1 or 2 on a text with too few runs, stating how many runs that tolerance needs. It throws the same error for any other tolerance, for a tolerance on a field that is not a pattern field, and for a tolerance in a filter without an `eq` test. Towards the pattern work cap, it counts one unit for each cell that it fills in the table of edit distances between the text and a value.

StringFilter.description: The engine tests a text field against this filter for equality, for a text range, or with the set, prefix, and pattern tests. On a `string[]`, `verbatim[]`, or `enum[]` field, the engine tests each element of the list on its own. A document passes `eq`, `in`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `contains`, `wildcard`, or `regex` when one element passes the test. However, a document passes `ne` or `nin` only when every element differs from the values. The engine applies the range tests `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, and `between` to a single `string` or `verbatim` field whose type includes `sortable`. It throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for a text range on any other field. It orders the values as a sort on the field does, so it compares their case folds first and compares their raw code points only where the folds are equal. A pattern field is a `verbatim` or `verbatim[]` field, or a `string` or `string[]` field whose type includes `pattern`. On a pattern field, the engine answers `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `nin`, `startsWith`, `endsWith`, `contains`, `wildcard`, and `regex` from the field's pattern index, and `caseFold` applies to each of those tests. The engine compares the code points of each value as they are stored, with no Unicode normalisation. On an `enum` or `enum[]` field, the engine answers `eq`, `ne`, `in`, `nin`, `startsWith`, and `endsWith` from the field's index of values. A `string` or `string[]` field whose type leaves out `pattern` keeps no index of whole values, so the engine throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` for those six tests, and for `matchesAny` and `containsAll`, on such a field. The engine also throws `SEARCH_INVALID_FILTER` in these cases: - The filter sets `contains`, `wildcard`, `regex`, or `caseFold` on a field that is not a pattern field. - The text or the pattern of a test on a pattern field holds more than 1,024 code points. - A literal test under `caseFold` has a text whose case fold holds more than 2,048 code points. - A `wildcard` or `regex` pattern breaks its syntax or one of its limits.

prefix.description: The returned terms complete this text.

limit.description: The lookup returns this many completions, most widely used first, and 10 by default.

term.description: This is the completed term, as the index holds it.

documentFrequency.description: The term appears in this many documents, which is what ordered the list.

terms.description: These completions run most widely used first.

elapsed.description: The lookup took this many milliseconds.

analysisStale.description: This turns true when the index's terms came from an older analysis than its language module produces now.

SuggestResult.description: What Narsil.suggest  returns: the indexed terms that complete a prefix, ready to offer as you-type suggestions.

SynonymRule.description: One rule of a synonym set, which IndexConfig.synonyms  and SynonymOperations.updateSynonyms  take as a list. The engine analyses every word with the language, the tokeniser, and the stop words of the index, so a rule that says `jackets` also matches `jacket` wherever the index stems the two alike. A set can hold up to 100,000 rules, 500,000 words, and 4,194,304 bytes of words in UTF-8.

synonyms.description: These rules make up the set, with every word as it was written, and an empty list removes the set.

SynonymSetBody.description: The body of `GET /indexes/{name}/synonyms`, and the body that `POST /indexes/{name}/synonyms` takes.

total.description: How many records the filters matched in total, across every page.

from.description: This page skipped this many records.

limit.description: This page asked for this many records.

next.description: Pass this back as `from` for the next page, and it is null on the last page.

TaskListPage.description: One page of task records, ordered newest first.

indexed.description: The server has indexed this many documents so far.

failed.description: The server has rejected this many documents so far.

bytesProcessed.description: The server has read this many bytes of the body so far.

bytesTotal.description: The body holds this many bytes in total.

TaskProgress.description: How far a running import has gone, which is what a progress bar reads. The byte counts describe the request body, so they give an honest fraction from the first batch onwards, while the document counts only cover what the server has already handed to the engine. Task types other than `import` report no progress.

id.description: This identifies the task, and is what you poll by.

type.description: This says which operation the task runs.

indexName.description: The operation runs against this index.

status.description: This says where the operation stands.

owner.description: Identifier of the server instance running this task; see ServerOptions.instanceId.

createdAt.description: The server accepted the task at this many milliseconds since the epoch.

startedAt.description: Work started at this many milliseconds since the epoch.

completedAt.description: Work ended at this many milliseconds since the epoch, and a task omits it until it reaches a final status.

cancelRequestedAt.description: A cancel arrived at this many milliseconds since the epoch, which is how a task still running shows that it is stopping.

progress.description: How far the work has gone, which an import reports and other task types omit.

result.description: What the work produced, which an `import` or `importExport` task reports once it finishes.

error.description: This says why the task failed, and a failed task alone carries it.

TaskRecord.description: One long-running operation, which the server answers with straight away and you then poll. Every route that starts a task answers with this same record, and `GET /tasks/{id}` returns it again as the work moves on.

TaskStatus.description: Where a long-running operation stands. A task starts `running`, because the server begins the work as it accepts the request. Where the server already drives ServerLimits.maxConcurrentTasks  tasks, it answers 429 `TOO_MANY_REQUESTS` and starts none. A task reaches `cancelled` only where the work itself stops early, so a cancel that arrives too late leaves the task `succeeded`.

TaskType.description: Which long-running operation a task record tracks.

words.description: The rule holds from 2 to 100 words, and each word must analyse to exactly one token.

TwoWaySynonymRule.description: A two-way rule makes every word in `words` a synonym of every other word in the rule, so a search for any one of them also matches documents that hold the others.

field.description: The request covers this vector field, and every vector field of the index where you leave it out.

threshold.description: The engine promotes the field to an HNSW graph once it holds this many vectors.

filterThreshold.description: A selectivity ratio between 0 and 1, defaulting to 0.03. A filtered search whose filter matches a smaller share of the graph's vectors scans just the matches, and one matching a larger share searches the graph. The engine clamps any value outside that range to it.

m.description: The graph keeps this many neighbours per node.

efConstruction.description: The engine explores this many candidates as it builds the graph.

hnswConfig.description: These settings shape the graph: neighbours per node, build-time exploration, and the metric that ranks results.

quantization.description: The engine codes the promoted vectors in this mode. When this is unset, it picks the mode by the field's dimension. Set `none` to rank by the vectors alone.

storage.description: The engine keeps the field's full-precision vectors here. When this is unset, it picks `disk` under filesystem durability and `memory` on every other engine.

VectorIndexConfig.description: Controls when a vector field moves from a brute-force scan to an HNSW graph, and how that graph is built. A small field answers faster from a brute-force scan, so the engine builds a graph only once the field holds enough vectors to earn one. Leave every field unset to accept the engine's own values.

fields.description: One entry describes each vector field of the index.

fieldName.description: This describes the named vector field.

tombstoneRatio.description: Tombstones make up this share of the graph's nodes, from 0 to 1. Before the first build, where VectorMaintenanceResult.graphCount reads 0, the engine divides by the number of stored vectors, because no graph exists yet.

graphCount.description: The field holds this many HNSW graphs: 0 before the first build and 1 once a graph exists.

bufferSize.description: This many vectors wait outside the graph, which a search scans one by one.

building.description: This stays true while a graph build runs.

waitingForMemory.description: This turns true while a rebuild that keeps recall up waits for the node to have room for a second graph beside the one it serves, and false once it starts.

estimatedCompactMs.description: Narsil.compactVectors  would take about this many milliseconds.

estimatedOptimizeMs.description: Narsil.optimizeVectors  would take about this many milliseconds.

VectorMaintenanceResult.description: The state of one vector field, and what maintenance would cost, as Narsil.vectorMaintenanceStatus  reports it. Removing a vector leaves a tombstone in the graph, and enough of them slow a search down. Read this to decide when compaction earns its cost.

field.description: Name of the schema field that holds the vector to compare against. Must reference a field declared as `vector[N]` in the index schema.

value.description: Raw query vector, given as a number array or a `Float32Array`. Length must match the indexed field's dimension or the search rejects the request with `VECTOR_DIMENSION_MISMATCH`.

text.description: Text to embed at query time using the index or instance embedding adapter. Mutually exclusive with `value`; requires a configured adapter.

similarity.description: Score floor applied during ranking. Hits scoring below this value are dropped before `limit` is enforced, so the returned hit count can be smaller than `limit` even when more documents exist. The floor is interpreted in score space for every metric; for `euclidean`, distance is mapped to a similarity score of `1 / (1 + distance)` first. Defaults to no floor.

metric.description: Similarity metric used for ranking. Defaults to `cosine`. Choose `dotProduct` for raw inner-product scoring on already-normalised vectors and `euclidean` for distance-based ordering.

efSearch.description: The engine keeps this many candidates as it walks the HNSW graph, so a higher value can find more of the true neighbours, although each query takes longer. The engine applies it only once the field holds a graph. The engine fetches k hits, where k is one more than the number of hits up to the end of the page, so k is `limit` plus 1 on a first page. When a query leaves `efSearch` unset, the engine keeps the larger of 50 and k plus a margin, where the margin is 50 below 768 dimensions, 75 from 768 to 1,023 dimensions, and 0 at 1,024 dimensions and above. Under a filter, the engine counts only the candidates that pass the filter.

oversample.description: The engine re-scores this many times k candidates in a quantized field against the full-precision vectors before it returns the best `limit`, where k is one more than the number of hits up to the end of the page, so k is `limit` plus 1 on a first page. For a value below 1, or for a value that is not a finite number, the engine throws a `NarsilError` with code `CONFIG_INVALID`. The engine ignores it on a field whose quantization is `none`. When a query leaves it unset, the engine sets the number of candidates that it re-scores from k and from the field's dimension. It rounds that number up, and it re-scores at least 3k candidates under `osq1` and `osq2`, and at least k under `osq4` and `osq8`. Below 768 dimensions, it re-scores 3.23k + 55.9√k under `osq1` and 2.6k + 22.5√k under `osq2`. From 768 to 1,023 dimensions, it re-scores 2.2k + 27√k under `osq1` and k + 16√k under `osq2`, and under `osq2` it re-scores at least the smaller of k + 75 and k + 18√k. At 1,024 dimensions and above, it re-scores 3k under both. Under `osq4`, it re-scores 5k below 1,024 dimensions and 2k from 1,024 dimensions, while under `osq8` it re-scores 2k at every dimension. Under a filter, the engine counts only the candidates that pass the filter. On vectors spread evenly across every dimension, a one-bit or two-bit code can find fewer than 95% of the true nearest neighbours at these defaults, so raise `oversample` on a query that needs more of them.

VectorQueryConfig.description: Vector-search inputs passed under `QueryParams.vector`. Supply either a raw `value` array or a `text` string for auto-embedding; passing both throws `EMBEDDING_CONFIG_INVALID`. Result count is governed by the outer query's `limit`, not by any field on this object.

version.description: The build came from this package version, or this is null where the build stamped none.

gitSha.description: The build came from this git commit, or this is null where the build stamped none.

dirty.description: This is true when the working tree held uncommitted changes at build time.

vectorSearch.description: The thread that answered searches vector graphs through the native search core under `native`, and through WebAssembly under `wasm`.

scaledOut.description: This is true while every worker holds a copy of the index.

reloadCount.description: The index has loaded its copies again this many times after an idle spell dropped them.

WorkerCopyReport.description: Whether one index holds worker copies at the moment Narsil.getMemoryStats  reads it, and how many times it has loaded them again after giving them up while idle.

wait.description: Setting this makes the write return only once every worker copy holding the index has applied it, so the next query sees it whichever copy answers. Leave it off for a load, and call DocumentWriteOperations.waitForWrites  once at the end.

WriteOptions.description: Per-write options every write accepts. A write returns once the main copy holds it, and it reaches the worker copies afterwards, so a query that a copy answers may come back without a write that returned before it.

Error.description: The server refused the request or failed to answer it.
